_comment: News of one month, newest day first. Written once a day by the scheduled task 'WoW Forever daily news (gear planner)'; nothing is ever deleted, this is also the changelog. Sections in this order when they have items: 'Game' (hotfixes, patch notes, fixed quests, announcements), 'WoWSims' (changes to the simulator). Every item: title, text (own words, one or two sentences), url, source, and tags. Tags, one to three per item, only from this list: Druid, Hunter, Mage, Paladin, Priest, Rogue, Shaman, Warlock, Warrior, Items, Dungeons, Quests, Professions, PvP, World, Races, Upcoming, WoWSims. A last section 'Gear Planner' holds the planner's own patch notes (tag 'Planner', source 'Gear Planner', no url; the News page shows it as a feed of its own); it is written when the site changes and must be kept when the day's news is added. Never mention the cheering figures (Bogdan, Afly, Larry) in the Gear Planner changelog: they are a surprise.

entries.summary: Blizzard's hotfix notes of 25 November rework Balance Druid talents, let Hunter and Warlock pets and Paladin's Exorcism crit again, tone down the Revelation enchant on area spells and change Alterac Valley to reward objectives. WoWSims updated its Warlock, Druid, Shaman and Hunter presets.

items.title: Balance Druid talents reworked
items.text: The hotfix of 25 November rebuilds part of the Balance tree. Improved Wrath is now Starlight Wrath and also shortens Starfire's cast by up to 0.5 seconds; Improved Moonfire is now Moon and Stars and protects Starfire from losing cast time when you are hit; Eclipse always adds up to 20% crit to Wrath; and Moonkin Form adds 10% Arcane and Nature damage. Moonfury is gone, replaced by Dreamstate, which gives you up to the full benefit of Innervate when you cast it on someone else.

items.title: Druids: Improved Starfire cut to 2 points, talents reset
items.text: Improved Starfire now has 2 ranks instead of 5, with an 8% or 15% chance. Druids who had 3 or more points in it had all talents reset and must spend them again. Also fixed: Hurricane lands its last hit, and Genesis now raises Hurricane damage and Tranquility healing.

items.title: Hunter and Warlock pets can crit again
items.text: Pets of both classes had no chance to crit with their plain melee attacks; that is fixed. For Warlocks the Succubus and Incubus lose 5% crit they had by mistake. Beast Mastery's Summoned Hawks get about 5% more crit, attack your target even when the pet is on Passive, and can be dismissed with Dismiss Pet or a right-click.

items.title: Paladin: Exorcism can crit, Judgements refresh
items.text: Exorcism could not crit and now can. Judgements on an enemy are refreshed by attacks again when under 20 seconds remain. Holy's Oath of Light lasts 60 minutes, and Libram of Law now affects Judgement of Command.

items.title: Shaman, Rogue and Warrior fixes
items.text: Chain Lightning now uses up Clearcasting when a Shaman has it together with 5 Maelstrom Weapon stacks. Poised is removed when a Rogue uses Sap or Distract from Stealth. The Arms talent Weaponmaster comes back properly after dying in a battleground.

items.title: Revelation weapon enchant procs less often on area spells
items.text: The Revelation enchant now rolls its proc once per wave of an area spell instead of once for every target hit, and it no longer covers the whole duration of a channeled spell. Casters who use it mainly on area damage get less out of it.

items.title: Item fixes: trinkets, a renamed totem
items.text: Blackhand's Breadth can no longer be resisted, Chained Essence of Eranikus no longer goes through immunities, and the Night Watchman's Torch works again while mounted or casting. Totem of the Storm is now called Totem of the Maelstrom, and Unerring Purpose sells to vendors for a proper price.

items.title: Official notes confirm the 24 November changes
items.text: Blizzard's notes now list what was seen yesterday: Blackblade of Shahram's haste buff goes to the wielder, and Rogue poisons and Blinding Powder bind on pickup, which Blizzard calls temporary while a bug is fixed. Paladins and Warlocks who finished their epic mount quest earlier can pick up Journeyman Riding for free from their quest giver.

items.title: Alterac Valley rewards objectives, not a rush
items.text: Killing the enemy General gives much less reputation and honor; towers, graveyards, mines, lieutenants and enemy NPCs give more reputation, and objectives slightly more honor. The long-match reputation bonus starts after 20 minutes instead of 60. All enemy NPCs are tougher, and Generals and their Warmasters or Marshals are stronger for 20 minutes unless objectives are taken. Blizzard expects about the same honor and more reputation per match. Unlooted Storm Crystals are no longer mailed to you.

items.title: Dungeon fixes: Blackfathom Deeps and Sunken Temple
items.text: The Altar of the Deeps in Blackfathom Deeps can be used again after 3 seconds and gives the Blessing of Blackfathom properly. In the Temple of Atal'Hakkar the Avatar of Hakkar should now always appear.

items.title: Legacy system fixes
items.text: Reinforce now cuts durability loss by 8% per rank, up to 40%. The Quick and the Dead makes Shadowform, Moonkin Form, Travel Form and Trueshot Aura free as intended. PvP Legacy achievements give credit at Exalted, and Lord Valthalak Laid to Rest gives its Legacy credit.

items.title: Quest and world fixes
items.text: Fixed or eased: the Horde version of the Hunter quest Saving the Best for Last, Encrypted Twilight Texts dropping for three Silithus quests, Blind Vengeance in Hyjal, the Smithing Tuyere quest in Searing Gorge (more Steamsmiths), and the Scarlet Subterfuge disguise now lasts an hour. Magram centaurs in Desolace respawn faster, and Alliance races can no longer declare war on the Kirin Tor or, for Dwarves, the Wildhammer Clan.

items.title: Warlock presets regeared
items.text: All five Warlock presets got new gear, among it Headmaster's Charge as the weapon in three of them, Belt of the Archmage, Robe of the Void, Burial Shawl and Rune Band of Wizardry.

items.title: New rotations for Cat Druid and Elemental Shaman
items.text: The Cat Druid preset has a largely rewritten rotation, including a rule for targets that cannot bleed, where Ferocious Bite is the only finisher. The Elemental Shaman rotation now keeps its totems up and uses a different elixir.

items.title: Balance Druid and Hunter preset changes
items.text: The Balance Druid preset now wears enchants on its gear, including Revelation on the weapon, and swaps its ring and weapons. The Beast Mastery and melee Survival Hunter presets no longer set a pet attack speed option.

items.title: Build plan opens with before and after
items.text: The head of Build plan is one big line: your equipped DPS, an arrow with the gain, the planned DPS. The simulator check has a card of its own next to it, "Next: check it for real", which turns green once the plan is checked. "How thorough" is four buttons instead of a dropdown. Undo and the reset say what they do, and "Rebuild the plan" is now called "Reset to the automatic plan": it drops your changes and the simulator's, locked slots stay.

items.title: Several groups in Group up
items.text: Group up can keep more than one group. A row of tabs at the top has one per group, with its name and how many characters are in it; "New group" starts one with your open character in it. Each group has its own members, a friend you paste joins the group that is open, and "Share the whole group" shares that one. Rename or delete a group at the right; deleting a group keeps its characters.

items.title: Smaller fixes
items.text: A battleground switched off under PvP now really takes its quartermaster's items out of the lists. Enchant names link to Wowhead with a tooltip. The preset buttons under Check gear fit their column. Build plan says when a locked slot keeps an item from content you switched off.

items.title: A new way through the planner
items.text: The steps are now: Check gear, Content Selection, Customize, Build plan, Farm it. What content you do has a page of its own, as one list to work through: dungeons, reputations, dungeon sets, set bonuses, PvP, quests, crafting, world drops, vendors. The plan is built as soon as you choose. Customize comes before Build plan: an item you pick by hand is locked, and "Check the plan with the simulator" builds around it. The tour and the FAQ follow the new order.

items.title: Build plan is one panel
items.text: What used to be three boxes is one: the fight, the guides, "Clear plan" and the stat weights sit under "More options", and enchants and professions are a fold right below your planned gear. A short key says what the cards show; slots where you already wear the planned item carry a green "You wear it" mark. Planned enchants show their icon. The to-do list is no longer repeated here: it is the first thing on Farm it.

items.title: Tidier lists everywhere
items.text: Check gear: the slot name stands above the item, the stat lines are gone (hover the item or its icon), and an enchant shows as icon and name. Customize: the slots are one row of item icons (gold is planned, green means a better option is open), and each option shows only its gain, with the stats in the hover of the number. Farm it and Group up: an open dungeon is a table with one line per drop and aligned columns. The healer panel shows its numbers as tiles, with the explanations behind question marks.

items.title: Themes are paused
items.text: The Classic theme is taken out for now and the Themes button is greyed out. Everybody sees the standard dark and gold look; a browser that had Classic chosen is put back to it. Themes will return later.

entries.summary: A hotfix on 24 November makes Blackblade of Shahram's haste proc speed up its wielder, binds Rogue poisons on pickup, and fixes long battleground queues on European PvE realms. WoWSims reworked its Balance Druid preset. Planner update: presets per character, the group plan as cards or list, an FAQ, and a changelog of its own.

items.title: Blackblade of Shahram: the haste proc now helps you
items.text: A hotfix seen on 24 November, for which Blizzard has posted no notes yet, changes Fist of Shahram, one of the spells the sword's spirit casts: the 30% attack speed now goes to the wielder instead of to the spirit itself. That makes the sword's proc worth more than before.

items.title: Stealthblade tooltip corrected
items.text: The dagger's Stealth effect is now described as lasting 20 seconds. Only the text changed; the effect already lasted that long.

items.title: Rogue poisons and Blinding Powder bind on pickup
items.text: Poisons and Blinding Powder a Rogue makes are now bound when picked up and vendors pay nothing for them, so they can no longer be traded or sold.

items.title: Epic class mounts teach the riding skill
items.text: Learning Summon Charger or Summon Forsaken Charger (Paladin) or Summon Dreadsteed (Warlock) now also teaches Journeyman Riding, so the mount can be used right away.

items.title: Quest fix: Lord Valthalak Laid to Rest
items.text: Lord Valthalak Laid to Rest now counts every version of the quest Saving the Best for Last that comes before it, including the Hardcore one.

items.title: Europe: long battleground queues on PvE realms fixed
items.text: Players on the European PvE ruleset were being matched in the Russian region by mistake, which made battleground queues much longer than they should be. Blizzard hotfixed it on 24 November; it takes full effect after a realm restart, such as the weekly maintenance of 25 November.

items.title: Preset changes: Balance Druid and Fire Mage
items.text: The simulator's Balance Druid preset was reworked: it is now a Windshaper Skyborne instead of a Night Elf, takes Leatherworking instead of Tailoring, and has new gear in 14 slots and a new rotation. The Fire Mage preset got a different main-hand weapon imbue.

items.title: Vilerend Slicer removed from the item list
items.text: The fist weapon Vilerend Slicer is no longer in the simulator's item data, so it can no longer be picked there.

items.title: The Watchers are out again, and "Got it" waits for the simulator
items.text: Players report that the faction The Watchers is not in the game yet. Its rewards are out of every plan and content choice again, also for characters that had it switched on; the tile under Reputations says "Not in the game yet". And while "Check the plan with the simulator" runs, the "Got it" buttons under Farm it and Group up are off, like the rest of the gear.

items.title: Check gear on one screen
items.text: The compact layout that was tried on the Dev copy is now on the Live site: four columns (slots, character details, stats, slots) with the weapons in a row below. Each slot is one row with icon, name, slot and one line of stats, and the enchant as a small button on the right. Click the icon to change an item. Talents are shown once, in the chip under the name; the second copy in Character details is gone.

items.title: Fit the estimate to your talents
items.text: When your talents are not the build's standard ones, Build plan shows "Fit the estimate to my talents". It measures the stat weights with the simulator for your talents and gear, which takes a few minutes, and rebuilds the plan with them. The measured weights belong to those talents: other characters of the same build keep the standard ones.

items.title: A hit target of your own
items.text: Build plan has a "Hit target" choice under the plan's numbers. The default is the cap, as WoWSims and the guides plan. A lower target, or none at all, makes the planner stop paying for hit earlier and spend those slots on other stats. Changing it rebuilds the plan.

items.title: Set the fight of the simulation
items.text: Sim setup, under "Buffs and fight": length of the fight, how much it varies, how many enemies and their level can be set, for example a 40 second fight against three level 60 enemies as in a dungeon. The default stays the fight WoWSims ships, and the page says so when yours differs.

items.title: Undo for the plan
items.text: Next to "Rebuild the plan" there is an "Undo" button. It takes back the last change of the plan, whether that was a rebuild, the simulator check, a swap by hand or a lock, up to 20 steps while the page is open.

items.title: No more sideways scrolling on a phone
items.text: On a narrow screen "Build plan" was almost twice as wide as the screen, so the whole page slid sideways. The plan cards, the check controls and the content rows now fit the width, and the notes behind question marks open across the screen.

items.title: Tell the planner where an item drops
items.text: Under an item whose source is missing or only guessed, "know where it drops?" (on a plan card: "Source?") opens a small window. Write what you know and either copy the report to paste it in a chat, which needs no account, or send it on GitHub. Reports are checked before they go in. The first one is in: Southern Watch Leggings come from the quest Snargl's Snout.

items.title: Item sources updated from AtlasLoot Continued
items.text: The planner now also reads the loot tables of the AtlasLoot Continued addon (by Okrah and Lag), next to AtlasLoot Classic Forever. 56 items that had no known source got one, 32 of them trash drops: 14 each in The Drowned City and Krol'dok Stronghold, 6 each in Blackmaw Hold and Alcaz Prison, 4 in The Shaper's Terrace, and single items in Zul'Farrak, Blackrock Spire, Dire Maul and the City of Dalaran. 24 more moved from a placeholder dungeon to the real one, now with the boss that drops them. Loot of the world bosses is known too; it counts as raid loot and stays out of the plan until raids are in.

items.title: Lock items in your plan
items.text: Every slot card under "Build plan" has a small lock. A locked item stays: "Rebuild the plan" and "Check the plan with the simulator" keep it and choose the other slots around it, so a locked piece with a lot of hit rating means less hit elsewhere. A note says which slots are locked and what that costs against a free plan, with "Unlock all". A lock on one hand holds both hands.

items.title: Classic theme rebuilt
items.text: Classic now has exactly the layout of Modern, piece for piece, and only changes the look: a night backdrop, a parchment workspace with dark ink, steel-blue bars, slate gear panes and crisp bronze frames. The old Classic with its menu at the left is gone.

items.title: Smaller character tiles
items.text: The tiles under the tabs are two lines high: name, then race icon, build and level. The faction shows as the coloured edge. More characters fit in one row.

items.title: Group up: friends stay on the group page
items.text: A character or group link pasted under "Group up" is saved as a friend: it counts in the group and no longer gets a tile among your own characters. The page lists "Your characters" and "Friends" separately; a friend can be removed or made yours, and one of your tiles can be turned into a friend.

items.title: Check gear: smaller slot cards, notes behind question marks, talents in the details
items.text: Slot cards are only as tall as their content, with the enchant right under the item. The notes under Build and Preset moved behind question marks, and Character details has a Talents button that opens the talent trees. The line with class and "pre-raid" under the site title is gone.

items.title: Sim setup: explanations behind question marks
items.text: The long notes under Talents, Consumables, Buffs and "What the sim runs" moved behind a small question mark next to each heading. Hover or tap it to read them.

items.title: Check gear: tidier head of the character sheet
items.text: Build, race and level sit in one quiet line under the name, the talents are one chip with a "Change" button, and "Copy character link" and "Build my gear plan" are two buttons of one height on the right.

items.title: The simulator check keeps running when you switch tabs
items.text: "Check the plan with the simulator" no longer stops when you open another tab. A bar on every page shows where it is and has a Stop button. While it runs, everything that would change its input is locked: worn gear, the plan, content, talents and Sim setup, and switching characters.

items.title: Bug report copies instead of saving a file
items.text: "Bug report" and "Report a problem" put the report on the clipboard, ready to paste. A file is only saved when the browser does not allow copying.

items.title: Group up: the glowing frame marks the open card
items.text: The gold frame used to sit on the first-ranked dungeon all the time, which looked like it was selected. Now the frame marks the card you opened; first place keeps its gold number.

items.title: Farm it lists the Tier 0 piece behind a Tier 0.5 upgrade
items.text: A Tier 0.5 piece comes from a questline that takes the Tier 0 piece of the same slot. When a Tier 0.5 piece is an upgrade or in your plan, Farm it now lists that Tier 0 piece at the boss that drops it, tagged with what it turns into.

items.title: Tidier plan cards
items.text: The slots of your plan are cards of one size, two to a row, with the same lines in the same order: item with a "Source" word (hover for where it comes from, click for Wowhead) and guide tags, the enchant and what it gives, the item it replaces, then option 1 and option 2. Click the icon to change a slot. Click an option's icon to plan that item instead.

items.title: Less text around the simulation
items.text: Build plan lost several lines of explanation. Damage breakdown and Sim setup sit side by side, the estimate note has a warning sign, and what "Check the plan with the simulator" does shows when you hover "Powered by WoWSims". The spell-book note is a small book sign with a number next to Sim setup; hover it to read it. Sim setup has a cog on its button.

items.title: The simulator check gets a second opinion on hit rating
items.text: Near the hit cap the quick estimate pays more for hit rating than the simulator does, so the really better items could sit too far down the list to be tried. "Check the plan with the simulator" now also runs each slot's two best items by a score in which hit counts for nothing.

items.title: Pictures in the to-do list
items.text: Every row under "To do, biggest gain first" starts with the icon of the item or the enchant.

items.title: One click back to the build's standard talents
items.text: When your talents differ from the ones the build was measured with, Build plan shows a button "Use the build's standard talents" next to the hint. Estimate and simulator then fit together again; Sim setup changes them back any time.

items.title: Content rows start folded, each with All on and All off
items.text: Every row under "What content do you do?" (dungeons, reputations, dungeon set pieces, set bonuses, PvP, everything else) starts folded. It shows how much of it counts as a number with a small bar, like 19/19, and has one switch with two sides: All on and All off. Open a row only for the finer choice. For dungeon set pieces the switch also covers the Tier 0.5 questline.

items.title: The plan says when it is only an estimate
items.text: Until the simulator has checked a plan, a box above the buttons says so and points to "Check the plan with the simulator". It goes away once the check has run, and comes back when the plan changes.

items.title: You choose how thorough the simulator check is
items.text: Next to "Check the plan with the simulator" there is a choice now: Quick (the 2 best items per slot), Normal (3), Thorough (5) or Very thorough (8). Deeper finds items the estimate ranks lower, and takes longer. The choice is remembered.

items.title: The simulator check looks twice
items.text: When the first round through the slots changed something, "Check the plan with the simulator" goes through them a second time. An item taken early, for example for its hit rating, is judged again against the set as it ended up.

items.title: Clearer lines next to the simulation buttons
items.text: The lines behind "Damage breakdown" and "Sim setup" are larger and bold, so it is clear what each button opens.

items.title: Spell ranks from books
items.text: The highest rank of some spells comes from a book that drops, not from a trainer: Flame Shock VI, Fireball XII, Serpent Sting IX, Eviscerate IX and others. Like wowsims.com, the simulation casts the trained rank for most builds, so the numbers stay comparable. A note under the simulation now says so and names the books; tick the ones you have learned in Sim setup and the simulation casts their rank, worth about 3 to 22 DPS depending on the spell.

items.title: The estimate says what it does not know about you
items.text: The estimate assumes the build's own talents, buffs, consumables and rotation. When yours differ (other talents, a WoWSims import with its own settings, changed buffs or consumables), a line under the estimate says so, and the "far apart" note names the reasons. "Measure for my character" under Stat weights makes the estimate fit you.

items.title: Sim setup moved next to the simulation
items.text: "Sim setup" is no longer in the top row. It is a button under the simulated numbers on Build plan and opens as a window, next to the numbers it changes.

items.title: Report a problem
items.text: "Report a problem" at the bottom of every page copies and saves what is needed to look into a problem: your characters with plan, content choice and sim setup, the site and simulator version, and the text of the page. Nothing is sent anywhere; you pass the file on yourself.

items.title: A nightly look for odd numbers
items.text: Every night the measured values are searched for things that deserve a second look: values that jumped, an enchant or item worth a lot to one build of a class and nothing to another that fights the same way, and things WoWSims' own set wears that measured as nothing. What is new goes into one report.

items.title: Content choice folds away
items.text: Dungeons, raids, reputations and set bonuses under "What content do you do?" are rows now. A row is shut while everything in it counts and says so ("all 19 count"); it opens when something is left out, or when you click "Choose". "Switch all on" turns a whole row on and shuts it.

items.title: The simulator check looks for the best set, faster
items.text: "Check the plan with the simulator" now starts by running your plan, the guides' sets and your worn gear against each other and goes on from the best. Every candidate gets a short run first and a longer one only when it is close, so clear losers cost little. Small gains from 1.5 DPS count, after a second, longer run confirms them. At the end the winner and the runner-up get a long run, and the note says when the two are equal.

items.title: The simulator check tries enchants and pairs
items.text: "Check the plan with the simulator" used to swap single items only. It now also tries the enchants of every slot (the worn one, the proc enchants, the next best) and pairs of slots changed together: both rings, both trinkets, both hands and slots that trade hit rating. It never ends below what you wear. It takes longer than before.

items.title: The tour shows for everybody once more
items.text: Because the tour now only stays away after its tick, everybody sees it again once, also those who finished it before.

items.title: Group cards: a real button
items.text: "Who wants what" on a dungeon card is a button now instead of underlined text.

items.title: The bar is a path now
items.text: The pages read from left to right in the order you use them: Check gear, Build plan, Customize, Farm it, with arrows between them, and Group up apart. Old names: Character, Plan, Upgrades, Farm plan, Group plan. Customize is the step you may skip. Each page of the path ends with a button to the next one.

items.title: Enchants moved into Build plan
items.text: The Enchants & professions page is now a section at the bottom of Build plan that opens on a click.

items.title: A tour for Group up
items.text: The first time you open Group up, a short tour shows how to bring friends in, who counts, the switches and the dungeon cards.

items.title: The tour comes back until you tick it off
items.text: Both tours now open on every visit until "Don't show this again" is ticked. "Take the tour" at the bottom of the page still starts them by hand.

items.title: Weapons count with the enchant that fits them
items.text: A weapon in the upgrade lists used to keep the enchant of the weapon it replaces, so a staff was counted with a one-hand enchant. Now every weapon that goes into an enchanted slot counts with the best enchant that can sit on it, in the lists, the plan and "Sim this". For casters this moves two-handers up a lot. Planning such a weapon plans the enchant with it.

items.title: News without a character
items.text: The News page opens before you have imported a character, like the FAQ.

items.title: A tour on your first visit
items.text: The first time you open the planner, a short tour points at the real things on the page: importing a character, the pages in the order you use them, settings and help. It has a "Don't show this again" tick, and "Take the tour" at the bottom of the page starts it again.

items.title: Plan page flags items from switched-off content
items.text: A plan made earlier could keep an item whose source you switched off afterwards, for example a crafted piece with only dungeons and quests chosen. Such items are now marked "not in your content", with a note that "Rebuild the plan" replaces them.

items.title: Proc enchants on the off hand count less
items.text: Weapon enchants with a proc (Fiery Weapon, Crusader and the like) were valued on the off hand as if they sat on the main hand, so plans for dual wielders put them there too eagerly. They now count with the off hand's smaller share, and the nightly measurement measures them on the off hand itself.

items.title: Themes renamed
items.text: The two themes are now called Modern (dark and gold) and Classic (the former "2006").

items.title: Fewer re-measurements after simulator updates
items.text: A simulator update that only changes single items, foods or one class's spells now re-measures only the builds that use them, instead of all of them. Updates to shared code still re-measure everything, and so does the nightly run.

items.title: Plan and Upgrades: one job each
items.text: The switch between "Slot by slot" and "Plan for me" is gone. The Plan page has the content choice, the best set for it, the planned items, the to-do list and the simulation. The Upgrades page is always slot by slot and overrides single slots of the plan. Stat weights, guide sets and the encounter moved to the bottom of the Plan page.

items.title: Enchants from Season of Discovery removed
items.text: 14 enchants that the simulator's database carries but WoW Forever does not have are out of the lists and plans, among them Grand Arcanist, Grand Sorcerer, Grand Crusader, Grand Inquisitor and Dismantle. 2H Weapon - Lesser Agility counts 15 agility as in the game.

items.title: Theme 2006: heavy gold frames
items.text: The theme got a new build: header, menu, page and gear panes each sit in a thick cast-gold frame with rivets and engraving, on dark planks and leather, with the page itself on paper. More room between things, a wider page for large screens, larger text.

items.title: Farm plan: filter and tags
items.text: The dungeon list can show every upgrade, only BiS or only what is in your plan; the totals follow. Every drop now carries a tag: in your plan, BiS, or alternative with its place in the slot (2nd best, 3rd best). The group plan names the place too.

items.title: Presets per character
items.text: One character can have several presets, each with its own build, worn gear and plan: one for fire, one for frost, one against beasts. Pick, create and delete them under Build on the Character page, or in the menu at the top of the gear panes at the side. They stay one tile in the character bar.

items.title: Group plan: cards and list
items.text: Dungeons show as cards or as a list, each with the drops as icons, the gain under them, who needs what, the total for the group and a priority. Cards stay in order; the details of an open card show below its row. Names carry a tag: planned, BiS or upgrade.

items.title: FAQ
items.text: A new page next to Sim setup and News: what the planner does, how to use it, where the numbers and the data come from, and where it stops.

items.title: Changelog of its own
items.text: News now has two feeds: WoW Forever and WoWSims, and this site's own changelog.

items.title: Content choice you can see
items.text: "What content do you do?" is now a bar you cannot miss, and dungeons, reputations and the other sources are tiles with a picture: lit when they count, grey when left out.

items.title: New switch: procs unknown
items.text: Items whose proc rate the simulator does not know are still off by default, but can now be switched on under "Everything else".

items.title: Encounter in plain sight
items.text: Enemy, creature and terrain show as three buttons on a card instead of one small button.

items.title: Upgrades page
items.text: The slots at the top show the item they hold and whether an upgrade is open. In the item rows, gains are green and losses red, and "Plan" is the gold button.

items.title: Planned swaps show their worth
items.text: A planned item now says what it gains over the item it replaces.

items.title: Smaller things
items.text: The "simulator was updated" note is a small box at the bottom, dungeons have their own icons, and Wit's Edge is back with a source.

items.title: Raids: coming soon
items.text: "What content do you do?" now lists the raids, greyed out. Once their loot is in the planner you switch them on there, and they count in Upgrades, Farm plan and Group plan.

items.title: Content choice open by default
items.text: "What content do you do?" starts open and stays how you leave it. Set bonuses are tiles too, and only the sets you can complete with the content you switched on are listed, with what each bonus gives.

items.title: Upgrades: calmer slot bar, clearer rows
items.text: The slot bar is plain again: a generic picture of the slot and its name. Item rows are separate cards with the quality colour at the left edge.

items.title: Presets show their build
items.text: The preset menus name the build of each preset, and a character's tile stays in its place in the bar when you make or open another preset.

items.title: Spell damage and healing in their own colours
items.text: In the item rows spell damage is violet and healing turquoise. On the Plan page, "What content do you do?" now comes before the simulation.

items.title: All slots in sight
items.text: The slot bar on the Upgrades page wraps into two rows instead of scrolling sideways.

items.title: PvP has its own group
items.text: The battleground factions moved from Reputations to a PvP group, next to the PvP switch and the rank limit. The PvP switch alone decides whether their rewards count.

items.title: Set bonuses: hover for the pieces
items.text: Hovering a set under "Set bonuses to count" shows its pieces with their stats, what the bonus is worth for your build, and a link to the bonus text on Wowhead.

items.title: Hide a planned item
items.text: A planned item now has "Hide" next to "Undo": it leaves the plan and every list in one click.

items.title: Themes, and the first one: 2006
items.text: A Themes button sits next to Sim setup, News and FAQ. The first theme, "2006", turns the site into a fan page of the early days: black and night-blue background, the page as warm parchment in a wooden frame with gold scrollwork in the corners, a menu of dark plates with gold letters at the left, dark bars with a gold curl and a plus or minus box, cream cards with brown ink, chapter titles in dark red, small Verdana.

items.title: Lists follow the simulator much faster
items.text: The measurements behind the lists no longer wait for the night and no longer redo everything. After a WoWSims update only the builds it touches are measured again: nothing for interface changes, one class for a class change, everything for a change to the shared rules. What arrives during a run is measured right after it. Once a night everything is measured anyway.

items.title: Hide worn items and guide picks
items.text: On the Upgrades page the item you wear and the WoWSims and Wowhead picks have a "Hide" too. The Group plan says how many dungeons "Planned items only" leaves out.

entries.summary: The 23 November hotfixes fix the Feralheart 4-piece bonus, halve Fengus' Ferocity and Darkmoon Faire buffs that were giving double, keep world buffs when you change areas, and repair several Priest, Warlock and Warrior bugs. In WoWSims, nine items with an unknown proc rate are simulated far too high.

items.title: Feralheart 4-piece bonus fixed
items.text: The Druid Feralheart 4-piece bonus now really gives 4 energy every second for 5 seconds. Cat Druids wearing four pieces should see the energy the tooltip promises.

items.title: Shadow Priest fixes
items.text: Dark Inspiration now gives the right Spirit bonus when Mind Flay triggers it, and Chastise can be cast in Shadowform. Mind Vision no longer sets off proc effects.

items.title: Intensity now works with Incinerate
items.text: The Destruction talent Intensity had no effect on Incinerate; that is fixed.

items.title: Mortal Strike needs its talent again
items.text: Warriors could use Mortal Strike from the spellbook without having the talent. The spell still shows there but only works with the talent point spent.

items.title: World buffs: two were doubled, and they no longer drop between areas
items.text: Fengus' Ferocity gave twice the intended spell power and Darkmoon Faire buffs twice their intended strength; both are back to the intended values, so buffed numbers go down a little. World buffs no longer fall off when you change areas, but still do when you enter a raid.

items.title: Fewer extra weapon procs
items.text: A few spells and abilities triggered weapon procs more often than they should. That is corrected, which slightly lowers the value of proc weapons for builds that used those abilities; Blizzard did not name them.

items.title: Obsidian Sentinel in Uldaman drops loot
items.text: The Obsidian Sentinel now drops its loot as intended.

items.title: Filcher's Cowl has no level requirement
items.text: The cloak Filcher's Cowl can now be worn at any level.

items.title: Cooking: clam dishes and Murloc Fin Soup
items.text: Six clam recipes (from Boiled Clams to Clam Linguine) now give the correct Well Fed bonus and are listed as Stamina food. Murloc Fin Soup was raised a food tier, so it restores more and gives a bigger Well Fed bonus.

items.title: Engineering and Leatherworking recipe fixes
items.text: The Goblin and Gnome Engineer's Renewal Gifts no longer show up as unusable question marks, learning Goblin Mortar now also teaches The Mortar: Reloaded, and the Centaur Hoofwarmers pattern can be learned.

items.title: Quest fixes
items.text: In the Wetlands, For Further Study now has rewards, and Uncovering the Past and Gleaning Our Future give Ironforge reputation. In Riverglades, Dunston Willis runs again near the end of his escort quest.

items.title: Wisp Form only for the dead
items.text: Living players can no longer end up in the Night Elf Wisp Form.

items.title: Nine items are simulated far too high: their proc rate is unknown
items.text: The game files give no trigger rate for the effects of Lord Sakrasis' Scepter, Gutrender, Frost Tiger Blade, Truesilver Champion, Dark Iron Sunderer, Bleakwood Hew, Ashbringer, Ichor Spitter and Darkblade, and WoWSims lists them as waiting for that data. Until it has it, the simulator triggers the effect on every hit or cast, so these items look much better than they are; the Scepter showed up as best caster off hand for that reason.

items.title: Group plan as its own page
items.text: The Group plan is a tab of its own now. Paste your friends' characters, or share everyone at once with one link.

items.title: Copy and paste characters
items.text: "Copy character (equipped + planned gear)" on the Character page gives a link with worn and planned gear. The links are about ten times shorter than before.

items.title: Presets straight from WoWSims
items.text: Talents, rotation, consumables and gear of every build now come from WoWSims' own presets and update with it. The site looks for a new WoWSims version every half hour.

items.title: Lists say how old their numbers are
items.text: Upgrades and Plan show when the values were measured. Each slot has "Check the top 5 with the simulator" for an exact answer.

items.title: Set pieces explain themselves
items.text: A set item now says how many pieces you would wear, what the set bonuses are worth for your build, and whether the number in front includes a bonus.

items.title: Items the simulator cannot value are hidden
items.text: Nine items whose effect has no known trigger rate in WoWSims are left out of the lists. They are listed here under "On the radar".

items.title: New tab bar
items.text: Full names instead of numbers, Sim setup and News as buttons at the top right, and buttons to jump to the top and bottom of the page.

items.title: Fixes
items.text: Pre-pull casts show on the cast time line, Mana Agate has its name in the damage breakdown, and "Set bonuses: none" in Plan for me works.

entries.summary: No new numbered hotfixes since 20 November, but Blizzard temporarily switched off looking inside lockboxes. WoWSims made the Druid dungeon set bonuses work in the simulator.

items.title: Lockboxes can no longer be peeked into, for now
items.text: A weekend hotfix removed the option to look inside a lockbox and take only part of its contents, reportedly to stop an exploit. Blizzard says this is temporary and that a proper fix will bring peeking and partial looting back, with no date given yet.

items.title: Wildheart and Feralheart set bonuses work
items.text: The Druid dungeon sets now restore energy on swings and rage when struck in the simulator, and the Wildheart 5-piece bonus is no longer marked as partly implemented.

items.title: Random suffix items pick their best suffix
items.text: A change named "random suffix best EP" was merged: going by its name, the simulator can now pick the suffix worth the most for a build.

entries.summary: Dungeon resets cut to 5 per hour, Stormshroud's 3-piece bonus weakened, fixes for Rogue and Warlock.

items.title: Stormshroud Armor 3-piece weakened
items.text: The set's energy proc now fires less often (3% instead of 4%) and gives back 18 energy instead of 30. That lowers the value of three Stormshroud pieces for Rogues and Feral Druids.

items.title: Dungeon resets halved
items.text: A character can now reset and enter each dungeon at most 5 times per hour instead of 10. Short farm runs for a single boss hit that limit sooner.

items.title: Rogue: Blade Flurry and Shank
items.text: For Combat, Shank's damage now also reaches the second target while Blade Flurry is up.

items.title: Warlock: Demonic Aegis loophole closed
items.text: Demonology could keep the talent's bonus on Demon Armor or Demon Skin after dropping the talent. Both are now removed when talents are unlearned.

items.title: Quest and world fixes
items.text: Witch Doctor Ti'ik in the Hinterlands drops a head for each group member, Gor'marok in Tanaris respawns faster, a pillar in Blackrock Spire no longer traps players, and the forge at the Summit of Eternity works.

entries.summary: Retribution's two-hand specialization fixed, the Seed Hybridizer is back, several quest fixes.

items.title: Paladin: two-hand specialization fixed
items.text: Retribution's Two-Handed Weapon Specialization now raises all Holy damage while a two-hander is equipped, which makes two-handers a little stronger for Retribution.

items.title: Skyborne and Tauren racial fixes
items.text: Skyborne get their riding discount at Honored reputation, and the Tauren's Cultivation works more reliably, Purple Lotus included.

items.title: Seed Hybridizer is back
items.text: The camping feature was switched on again with changed values and a chance to fail; scarce herb seeds can no longer go into it.

items.title: Dungeon fixes
items.text: The Shade of the Archmage in Dalaran no longer vanishes when the fight starts, and Vitrix in the Shaper's Terrace hits less hard with Poison Shock.

items.title: Quest and item fixes
items.text: The parchment for "Stormpike's Deciphering" can be had again after destroying it, "Hunting for Ectoplasm" counts the right creatures, Motes of Unstable Magic are now soulbound, and Mosh'gra in the Riverglades can drop rare loot.

entries.summary: Upper Blackrock Spire made harder again, Soulforge tank set changed, many Shen'dralas quest fixes.

items.title: Upper Blackrock Spire back to intended difficulty
items.text: Enemy health and damage in Upper Blackrock Spire were raised to where they were meant to be. Expect slower runs for the loot there.

items.title: Item changes: Soulforge, staves, a torch
items.text: The Paladin's Soulforge Armor trades Strength for Spell Power, Whiteout Staff and Crackling Staff now have the same stats, and Shadow Priests can hold the Night Watchman's Torch.

items.title: Shaman: Flurry and Windfury Totem
items.text: Flurry no longer loses stacks when Windfury Totem attacks land.

items.title: Shen'dralas and other quest fixes
items.text: In Shen'dralas, pylon repairs and the Heart of Crystal count for the whole party and Spectral Iron Ore spawns more often and can be tracked. More Fen Creepers and Gravelsnout kobolds spawn for their quests.

items.title: Professions
items.text: Several Blacksmithing recipes and turn-ins were fixed, Cultivation works on Mageroyal, and the Waylaid Crate no longer gives an outdated reward.

items.title: PvP
items.text: Alterac Valley quests now need level 58, and mounting in the Warsong Gulch starting rooms is blocked.

entries.summary: Windfury Totem reworked, Vampiric Embrace change announced, Fury Warrior fixes.

items.title: Shaman: Windfury Totem reworked
items.text: The totem's extra attacks now respect armor, have an internal cooldown and generate Rage. Several abilities (Mutilate, Execute, Shield Slam and others) no longer trigger extra Windfury attempts. Maelstrom Weapon can no longer benefit two casts.

items.title: Upcoming: Vampiric Embrace halved for the group
items.text: With the weekly maintenance, Vampiric Embrace heals for 10% of the Shadow damage instead of 20%, while the Priest gets double. Solo play does not change. Dark Inspiration also stopped stacking from several Shadow Priests.

items.title: Warrior: Fury fixes
items.text: Cleave and Heroic Strike now trigger Unbridled Wrath and Reckless Swings and no longer use up Flurry stacks.

items.title: Rogue and Druid fixes
items.text: Poison ranks are capped at their highest rank and Shank no longer removes combo points from other targets. Wild Growth ranks go on cooldown properly, and Genesis raises the damage of Pounce's bleed.

items.title: Items and enchants
items.text: The reputation formula for Enchant Boots - Speed is bind on pickup, Outrider's Gloves work, and the Violet Tragan no longer breaks crowd control.

items.title: Dungeon and quest fixes
items.text: The Abyssal Bubble in the Drowned City can no longer block, dodge or parry; Sunken Temple's statues stay usable after a wrong order. Blood Red Bandanas drop more often and Witch Doctor Zum'rah spawns reliably.

entries.summary: Many item stat corrections (the Bad Hat, Channeler's Ring), Windfury from all melee, Wild Growth doubled.

items.title: Item stat corrections
items.text: A batch of items had their stats fixed, among them the Bad Hat (spell power), Everstaring Abomination Eye (Spirit), the Darkspear signet rings (Mp5) and Souvenir Sea Shell. Taran Icebreaker is now a two-handed mace, and the Glimmering Mithril Insignia no longer needs mail.

items.title: Channeler's Ring and Blessed Band of Light
items.text: Channeler's Ring now has Spell Power instead of Spirit and Blessed Band of Light lost its Hit. Until raids open, the Band can be swapped one way for the Ring at Pix Xizzix's vendor.

items.title: Shaman and Paladin: Windfury and Judgement
items.text: Windfury Totem now procs from all main-hand melee abilities, not from off-hand-only strikes. Judgement of Command counts as melee again and triggers on-hit effects; the other Judgements stay ranged.

items.title: Druid: Wild Growth
items.text: Restoration's Wild Growth heals for twice as much from spell power (6.6% instead of 3.3%) but can no longer be cast while moving.

items.title: Other class fixes
items.text: Stuns on creatures have diminishing returns again, Frost Nova breaks on proc and Blizzard damage, Berserker Rage removes Sap, and Siphon Life rank 1 cannot be cast while silenced.

items.title: Dungeons
items.text: Enemies that are trivial for a party member give no experience, non-boss enemies in the Drowned City respawn after 2 hours instead of 1, and Sneed in the Deadmines ejects properly.

items.title: Quest fixes
items.text: Many quest items now drop for every eligible party member, Rogues reach the right Zul'Farrak for "The Talisman of Kazdor", and several Riverglades and Feralas quests were repaired.

entries.summary: Judgement becomes a ranged attack, Volley stops triggering procs, tailoring bags changed.

items.title: Paladin: Judgement is a ranged attack
items.text: Judgement no longer counts as a melee attack: it uses ranged hit chance and does not trigger melee item procs. Unsealed Fury also stopped creating Windfury Totem echoes.

items.title: Hunter: Volley
items.text: Volley no longer triggers procs and stops channeling when the Hunter moves.

items.title: Druid, Priest and Shaman fixes
items.text: Rend and Tear works on Pounce's bleed, Confounding Flash and Twilight Focus work in Shadowform, and a bug with Flametongue Totem rank 2 was fixed.

items.title: Items
items.text: Earthen Silk Slippers no longer raise spell damage too much, and Bloody Claws of Attack give the right fist weapon skill.

items.title: Tailoring bags
items.text: Five bag recipes changed in bolts needed and slots, for example the Red Mageweave Bag at 5 bolts and 14 slots.

items.title: Riverglades and quest fixes
items.text: Several Riverglades enemies hit much less hard. "Scarlet Diversions", "The Giant in the Den" and "Freedom for All Creatures" can be completed again. Item Restoration was switched off while a bug is looked into.

entries.summary: Enhancement Shaman and Affliction Warlock retuned, Hunter pets weaker, gold on high-level quests.

items.title: Shaman: Enhancement retuned
items.text: Stormstrike hits harder on a longer cooldown, Mental Dexterity turns less Intellect into attack power, and Maelstrom Weapon was reworked. Blizzard's aim is to favour Windfury over spell power and Intellect, which changes what gear Enhancement wants. Weapon imbues and totems can now be used together.

items.title: Warlock: Affliction and pets
items.text: Wrack does 30% less damage and instead speeds up damage-over-time ticks while channeled; Soul Siphon counts Corruption, Siphon Life and Bane of Agony for up to 36%. Imp, Voidwalker, Incubus and Succubus have about 15% more health.

items.title: Hunter: pet health bug and Hawk
items.text: Pets had 150% of their normal health by mistake and are now at 115%. Arcane Shot and Summon Hawk cost 11% of base mana, and the Hawk's melee damage went up by about 80%.

items.title: Other class fixes
items.text: Nature's Swiftness makes Wild Growth instant, the Revelation enchant no longer triggers from Vampiric Embrace healing, Bane of Havoc triggers the global cooldown, and Sweeping Strikes keeps its charges without a second target.

items.title: Items
items.text: Rage of the Storm (Shaman quest reward) now has Strength instead of Intellect and a 3.6 speed, Sparklance Wand deals Arcane damage, and racial vendor mounts are bind on pickup.

items.title: Gold from quests at level 48 and up
items.text: Most quests from level 48 now also pay gold, apart from repeatable ones and those with valuable item rewards.

items.title: Professions
items.text: Lesser Spirit enchants now really give Spirit, the Arcane Salvager works for lower-level enchanters, Swiftstrike Shot and Swiftfeather Arrow are tradable, and Greater Firepower was renamed Holy Power.

entries.summary: Dungeon experience up 50%, the Drowned City made easier, class and quest fixes across the board.

items.title: Dungeons: more experience, easier Drowned City
items.text: Kills in dungeons give 50% more experience. In the Drowned City a bug that added about 30% damage was fixed and the Deathless Marrow fight was toned down. Zarla Ober in Alcaz Prison now drops loot, and the Shaper's Terrace loot was fixed.

items.title: Class fixes
items.text: Arcane Concentration's chance is now split across a cast and its bolts, Flamestrike's ground ticks no longer use Clearcasting, Lightning Overload's damage on Lightning Bolt was fixed, Incinerate is limited to Destruction, and Power Infusion stays on allies.

items.title: Feral Druid and Hunter fixes
items.text: Feral Charge in Cat Form puts the Druid in combat at once and Natural Instinct applies to Lacerate and Pounce. Hunters no longer pull enemies from far away by targeting them.

items.title: Items
items.text: Berdun's Trusty Rifle lost its random stats and is no longer bind on equip, Gloves of Holy Might were fixed, and Waylaid Crates and Craftsman's Writs now drop in dungeons.

items.title: Quest fixes
items.text: Several quest items are now shared with the whole party, and around a dozen quests that could get stuck were repaired, among them "Jom-jom's Escape", "Fetch 'n' Fletch" and "Feathers in Flight".

items.title: World and PvP
items.text: Player numbers per zone were lowered in crowded zones, more so on PvP realms, and an invisible wall on the Alliance base roof in Warsong Gulch was removed.

entries.summary: First round of class fixes after launch, Voidwalker health raised, many quest repairs.

items.title: Class fixes
items.text: Bloom heals its target, Arcane Blast lasts its 18 seconds, the Voidwalker has more base health, and Soul Siphon no longer raises Wrack's own damage.

items.title: Items and professions
items.text: Searing Dagger only triggers from damaging spells. The Leatherworking Tanning Rack needs skill 125.

items.title: Dungeons
items.text: Zaetar's Spirit appears after Princess Theradras in Maraudon, and creatures in Blackmaw Hold and the Drowned City no longer break off the fight by mistake.

items.title: Quest fixes
items.text: About ten quests were repaired or eased, among them "Vorsha the Lasher", "The Sleeper Has Awakened" and "Rediscovering the Light"; Riverglades quest items are shared in a party.

items.title: Races
items.text: Shadowmelded Druids no longer get Ravage or Pounce, and the Orc's Command no longer raises some Warlock pets too much.

entries.summary: Small fixes the day after launch.

items.title: Launch-day fixes
items.text: Trade vendors sell apprentice bags, a Druid trainer was added, a few creatures respawn faster for their quests, and the Tauren's Plainsrunning no longer stacks in battleground preparation or works while carrying a flag.
